Recent reports indicate that credit card delinquencies have reached a notable level, with 12.8% of balances over 90 days past due, according to the New York Fed. However, a closer look reveals a distinction between overall delinquency rates, which include aged debts, and new delinquency rates, which have remained stable since 2024. The economic landscape shows a divide between consumers, where lower-income households experience significant credit stress amidst a backdrop of increasing spending concentration towards higher earners.

 - 12.8% of credit card balances are reported as overdue, marking the highest since 2008, but this includes outdated charged-off debts.
 - The current situation depicts a bifurcated consumer landscape where lower-income households face credit stress while higher-income individuals continue to drive consumer spending.

Source: https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/consumer-credit-stress-what-data-really-shows
